pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Wanderer above the Sea of Fog — the man standing alone on the dark rock with his back to us, leaning on his stick in a long green coat, and in front of him nothing but the white fog lying over the whole valley with the far peaks standing out of it, why O LORD do You stand far off, why do You hide in times of trouble
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_wanderer_above_the_sea_of_fog

pictures.scene: Sebastian Vrancx, Soldiers Plundering a Farm — a musket barrel thrust in at the farmhouse door, the woman in the red skirt crying out with her small child beside her throwing up both hands, a man on his knees pleading on the floor and another bolting out of the doorway with his mouth open, in pride the wicked pursue the needy, let them be caught in the schemes they devise
pictures.name: pd_vrancx_soldaten_plunderen_een_boerderij

pictures.scene: Marinus van Reymerswaele, The Money Changer and His Wife — the man in his great fur hat leaning over the green table with the scale-beam pinched between his fingers, the fat money bag and the piles of silver and gold coin lying out in front of him, his wife bent in close at his shoulder watching every coin, for the wicked man boasts in the cravings of his heart, he blesses the greedy and reviles the LORD
pictures.name: pd_reymerswaele_merchant

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Little Tower of Babel — the tower filling the whole sky, tier on tier of arches climbing out of the bare ground, the upper storeys still raw red brick and hung with scaffolding and cranes, a cloud drifting across it halfway up and tiny workmen crawling over every level, in his pride the wicked man does not seek Him, in all his schemes there is no God
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_tower_of_babel_rotterdam

pictures.scene: Karl Friedrich Schinkel, Castle by the River — the great house standing high up on its wall of rock with the battlemented walk running down from it, the terraced gardens and the stag on the paving below, the little town crowded at the water's edge and the river going off bright into the evening, he is secure in his ways at all times, Your lofty judgments are far from him
pictures.name: pd_schinkel_castle_river

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Parable of the Rich Fool — the old man alone in the dark room in his fur cap and spectacles, holding a coin up to the one candle he has lit, the gold counted out on the table beside the money bags and the ledgers and papers piled all around him, he sneers at all his foes, I will not be moved
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_parable_of_the_rich_fool

pictures.scene: The Laughing Fool — the jester in his yellow eared hood laughing wide open with all his teeth showing, one hand spread flat over his eye and the other holding up the bauble with its little carved head shouting beside him, from age to age I am free of distress, his mouth is full of cursing deceit and violence
pictures.name: pd_the_laughing_fool

pictures.scene: Joost Cornelisz Droochsloot, The Village — the wide dirt road running in between the thatched cottages to the church tower, villagers standing about in little knots all down it, some sitting on the bank, a dog trotting across the front and a group of women talking at the edge of the road, trouble and malice are under his tongue, he lies in wait near the villages
pictures.name: pd_droochsloot_dorp

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Taking of Christ — Judas with his hand clamped on Christ's shoulder, leaning in out of the dark to kiss Him while the soldier's black steel arm reaches across them both and the fleeing disciple throws back his head crying out behind, Christ standing still with His eyes down and His hands locked together, in ambush he slays the innocent, his eyes watch in stealth for the helpless
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_taking_of_christ

pictures.scene: George Stubbs, Horse Frightened by a Lion — the pale horse wheeling away from the rocks with its mane and tail flying, head twisted round and nostrils open, staring back at the dark scrub on the bank where something it cannot see is waiting, he lies in wait like a lion in a thicket, he lurks to seize the oppressed
pictures.name: pd_stubbs_horse_frightened_by_a_lion

pictures.scene: Winslow Homer, The Herring Net — the fisherman in oilskins and a sou'wester bent right over the side of the dory in the grey swell, hauling the net up out of the water hand over hand with the caught herring hanging silver all along the meshes, he catches the lowly in his net, they are crushed and beaten down
pictures.name: pd_homer_the_herring_net

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Beggars — the crippled men on the grass by the brick wall, one with his mouth open looking up and another dragging himself along on pads and crutches with foxtails pinned to his coat, a woman walking off behind them with the begging bowl, the helpless fall prey to his strength, God has forgotten
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_beggars

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Christ in the Storm on the Sea of Galilee — the little boat driven up on its side with the bow buried in white water, one man clinging to the rigging and another hauling at the torn sail while the rest crouch down in the stern, Christ sitting quiet among them in the dark as they wake Him, He hides His face and never sees, arise O LORD lift up Your hand O God
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_christ_in_the_storm_on_the_sea_of_galilee

pictures.scene: Gabriel Metsu, The Sick Child — the woman sitting with the limp child laid across her lap in a yellow jacket and a white shift, holding its small hand and looking down into its face, the child staring out dull-eyed and spent, the crucifixion picture hanging on the bare wall behind them, do not forget the helpless, why has the wicked man renounced God
pictures.name: pd_metsu_the_sick_child

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Belshazzar's Feast — the king in his gold brocade mantle and jewelled turban twisting round from the banquet table with his eyes wide and his arm flung out, knocking over the vessel in front of him, the grapes and the plate spilling on the cloth, You will never call me to account, but You have regarded trouble and grief
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_belshazzars_feast

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Elderly Man in Prayer — the old man in a plain brown robe out of the dark with his grey hair and full white beard, his eyes closed and his worn hands pressed flat together, the open book lying in the light on the table in front of him, You see to repay it by Your hand, the victim entrusts himself to You
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_elderly_man_in_prayer

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Jacob Blessing the Children of Joseph — the dying old man propped up in his white shirt on the red bed, reaching out to lay his hand on the fair boy's head while Joseph in his turban leans over him and the second child watches from the bedside, You are the helper of the fatherless, break the arm of the wicked and evildoer
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_jacob_blessing_the_children_of_joseph

pictures.scene: Thomas Cole, The Deluge — the drowned world seen out of a gap in the rocks, the flood lying flat and pale to the horizon with only bare crags left standing out of it, the ark floating far off in the haze, dead roots and a bleached skull on the stones in front, call him to account for his wickedness, until none is left to be found
pictures.name: pd_cole_deluge

pictures.scene: Christ Pantocrator, Sant Climent de Taull — the Romanesque apse painting of Christ enthroned inside the great mandorla on its blue ground, one hand raised in blessing and the other holding the open book that reads I am the light of the world, the cross set in the halo behind His head, the LORD is King forever and ever, the nations perish from His land
pictures.name: pd_taull_pantocrator

pictures.scene: Nicolaes Maes, An Old Woman Praying — the old woman in her white cap and black jacket with her hands folded and her eyes lifted, saying grace alone at the red-covered table with the open book, her spectacles and the little ink pot laid in front of her, You have heard O LORD the desire of the humble, You will strengthen their hearts and incline Your ear
pictures.name: pd_maes_an_old_woman_praying

pictures.scene: Edward Hicks, The Peaceable Kingdom — the little child in a white shift and red sash standing under the vine with his arm laid over the lion's shoulders, the ox and the lamb and the leopard lying down quietly around his bare feet, to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed, that the men of the earth may strike terror no more
pictures.name: pd_hicks_peaceable_kingdom

lines.text: Why, O LORD, do You stand far off?
Why do You hide in times of trouble?
In pride the wicked pursue the needy;
let them be caught in the schemes they devise.
For the wicked man boasts in the cravings of his heart;
he blesses the greedy and reviles the LORD.
In his pride the wicked man does not seek Him;
in all his schemes there is no God.
He is secure in his ways at all times;
Your lofty judgments are far from him.
He sneers at all his foes.
He says to himself, “I will not be moved;
from age to age I am free of distress.”
His mouth is full of cursing, deceit, and violence;
trouble and malice are under his tongue.
He lies in wait near the villages;
in ambush he slays the innocent;
his eyes watch in stealth for the helpless.
He lies in wait like a lion in a thicket;
he lurks to seize the oppressed;
he catches the lowly in his net.
They are crushed and beaten down;
the helpless fall prey to his strength.
He says to himself, “God has forgotten;
He hides His face and never sees.”
Arise, O LORD! Lift up Your hand, O God!
Do not forget the helpless.
Why has the wicked man renounced God?
He says to himself, “You will never call me to account.”
But You have regarded trouble and grief;
You see to repay it by Your hand.
The victim entrusts himself to You;
You are the helper of the fatherless.
Break the arm of the wicked and evildoer;
call him to account for his wickedness
until none is left to be found.
The LORD is King forever and ever;
the nations perish from His land.
You have heard, O LORD, the desire of the humble;
You will strengthen their hearts and incline Your ear,
to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed,
that the men of the earth may strike terror no more.
